# CLI reference

Update GitHub/Gitea/Forgejo Actions, Go module, container image, npm and Cargo dependencies.

```
deps [command] [flags]
```

deps finds the dependencies of a repository (GitHub/Gitea/Forgejo Actions, Go modules, container images, npm packages, Rust crates, Python packages and custom-annotated versions), looks up newer versions, and either prints the changes as a diff (`plan`), writes them (`apply`), or pushes one branch and opens one pull request per dependency or group (`run`). Files are edited byte-exactly and never reformatted.

The configuration is read from `.deps.yaml` (or `.deps.yml`) in `--dir`; `deps schema` prints its JSON Schema. With `--renovate`, the repository's Renovate config is translated instead (`deps migrate` writes that translation to `.deps.yaml`). Results go to stderr, diffs and explanations to stdout. See `deps help output`, `deps help environment` and `deps help exit-codes`.

Hidden flags for profiling: `--cpuprofile <file>` writes a CPU profile, and `--memprofile <file>` writes an allocation profile on exit (pprof format).

## Global flags

Every command accepts these flags.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--color` | string | `"auto"` | color stderr: auto (on a terminal, unless $NO_COLOR is set or $TERM is dumb; $CLICOLOR_FORCE or $FORCE_COLOR force it), always, never |
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (default: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--log-format` | string | `"auto"` | log format: auto (actions on a GitHub/Gitea Actions runner, pretty on a terminal, else text), pretty, text, json, actions (pretty records without elapsed time, colored, plus workflow commands: annotations, log groups); $DEPS_LOG_FORMAT replaces the default |
| `--log-level` | string | `"warn"` | log level: debug, info, warn, error; $DEPS_LOG_LEVEL, then $RUNNER_DEBUG=1 (debug) replace the default |
| `--renovate` | bool | `false` | compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |
| `--report` | string | `""` | plan, apply, run: also write the result as JSON to this file (see deps help output; default: $DEPS_REPORT) |
| `-v, --verbose` | bool | `false` | also print skipped dependencies (skip lines) |

## deps apply

Write the updates to the files, including go mod tidy, package-lock.json and Cargo.lock.

```
deps apply [flags]
```

Resolves every dependency, prints the same report as `deps plan` on stderr, and writes the changed files, including `go mod tidy` output (`go.mod`, `go.sum`), regenerated `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` or `Pipfile.lock`, `Cargo.lock` updated with `cargo update`, `Gemfile.lock` updated with `bundle lock`, `composer.lock` updated with `composer update`, `Manifest.toml` updated with Julia's Pkg, `MODULE.bazel.lock` updated with `bazel mod deps`, and the `--hash` lines of requirements files (pip-compile/`uv pip compile` output is regenerated from its header command, other files get the new release's hashes from the index). An update of a pip-compile input (`requirements.in`) rewrites the input and regenerates every compiled file named after it. Post-processors run on temporary copies; a failed one drops that module's or lockfile root's changes and is reported as an error. An update a post-processor finds inapplicable (a compiled requirements file whose inputs do not admit the version, a Go module version that declares another path) is left out instead, and the other updates of its files are applied: it is reported as `skip    <file>:<line>  <name>  <from> -> <to>  (cannot be applied: <reason>)`, counts as skipped, and is no error.

A dependency with updates in several PR buckets contributes one update to the files: the newest non-major one, else the lowest major. Its other updates are reported with `, separate PR`, as is the lock file maintenance update (`lockFileMaintenance`), which only `deps run` makes.

The `postUpgradeTasks` of the config run in `--dir` after the files are written, in the order `run` uses, when `--allow-tasks` (or `$DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS`) allows each of their commands. Otherwise nothing is written and the error names the first command not allowed. With `files` globs, every other file below `--dir` the commands changed is restored to its state before them (ignored files are left alone).

The platform is only detected from CI environment variables. Locally, lookups run without a platform token unless one of the token variables is set (see `deps help environment`).

### deps apply examples

```sh
deps apply && git diff --stat
```

### deps apply flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--allow-tasks` | strings | `[]` | postUpgradeTasks command allowed to run, `*` matching any text but ; & \| ` $( and line breaks, e.g. `go generate ./...`, `make *` or `*` (repeatable); they run repository code on this machine (default: $DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS, one per line) |

## deps completion

```
deps completion [command]
```

Generate the autocompletion script for deps for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

Subcommands:

- [`deps completion bash`](#deps-completion-bash): Generate the autocompletion script for bash
- [`deps completion fish`](#deps-completion-fish): Generate the autocompletion script for fish

## deps completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for bash.

```
deps completion bash
```

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(deps completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	deps completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/deps

#### macOS:

	deps completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/deps

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

## deps completion fish

Generate the autocompletion script for fish.

```
deps completion fish
```

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	deps completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	deps completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/deps.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

## deps completion powershell

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

```
deps completion powershell
```

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

The script registers the completer for the command named like the script file, so save it
as deps.ps1:

	deps completion powershell > deps.ps1

To load completions in your current shell session, run it:

	. ./deps.ps1

To load completions for every new session, run it from your powershell profile.

## deps completion zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for zsh.

```
deps completion zsh
```

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(deps completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	deps completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_deps"

#### macOS:

	deps completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_deps

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

## deps explain

Explain the rules, candidates and decision for each matching dependency.

```
deps explain <name-glob>...
```

Resolves only the dependencies whose name matches any of the doublestar globs (the syntax of rule `names`, for example `'actions/*'` or `'k8s.io/*'`) and prints, per occurrence, the matching rules, the effective policy, the rejected candidates by reason and the resulting update. The report goes to stdout, one block per occurrence:

```
actions/checkout  .gitea/workflows/ci.yml:10  (github-actions, action, git-tags, tag)
  current   v7.0.1
  rules     none
  policy    pin=keep allow=- updates=major,minor,patch,digest,pin group=- schedule=always minAge=-
  candidates 68
  rejected  not newer: 58 (v7.0.1, v7.0.0, v6.1.0, ...)  precision: 7 (v7, v6, v5, ...)  invalid: 2 (v2-beta, v6-beta)  prefix: 1 (1.0.0)
  result    up to date

github.com/spf13/pflag  go.mod:28  (gomod, indirect, go, go)
  current   v1.0.10
  rules     none
  policy    pin=keep allow=- updates=major,minor,patch,digest,pin group=- schedule=always minAge=-
  result    skipped: ignored by default (indirect; enable with a rule setting ignore: false)
```

The header names the manager, dep type, datasource and versioning. The other lines in a block:

- `age       released <date>` follows `current` when a `currentAge` rule needed the release time of the current version; `age       unknown (currentAge rules do not match)` when the datasource does not know it.
- `builtin   monorepo <name> -> group "<name> monorepo"` appears for monorepo members.
- `rules` lists the matching rules as `#<i> <fields> (from <file>:<line>)`, or `none` when no rule matched. `<i>` counts the rules of the whole config, those of `extends` first; `<file>` is where the rule is written: the config file (`.deps.yaml`, or the `--config` path), or an extended file as `<repo>//<path>[#<ref>]` (`(from org/deps-config//.deps.yaml:12)`). Rules with `updateTypes` that applied to an update follow as `#<i> <fields> (applies to <type>, from <file>:<line>)`.
- `policy` is followed by one `<type>: <policy>` line per such type. `versioning=` is appended when a rule set it.
- `rejected` groups versions by reason, most frequent first, with up to 3 newest examples each. Reasons include `ignored by rule #4 for major`, `outside allow /^\d+\.\d+$/`, `update type major not allowed`, `too new (released 2026-11-01, minimum 28 days)`, `release time unknown (minimum 28 days, timestamp-required)`, `older than current`, `above latest` (npm: a major above `dist-tags.latest`'s), `prerelease`, `precision` and `not newer`. The policy's `minAge=` reads `28 days (timestamp-required)` under `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-required`.
- `result` reads `skipped: <reason>`, `error: <err>`, `up to date`, or one `update` line per PR bucket, for example `update v6.0.0 -> v7.0.1 (major, bucket major)`.
- Each advisory is printed as `security  <id>  <summary>  <url>`.

Errors go to stderr as `error   <msg>`. A glob that matches no dependency fails with `no dependency matches <globs>` (exit 1). No globs, or an invalid glob, exits 2.

### deps explain examples

```sh
deps explain 'actions/*'
deps explain 'k8s.io/**' github.com/spf13/cobra
```

## deps migrate

Translate the Renovate config into .deps.yaml.

```
deps migrate [flags]
```

Translates the repository's Renovate config into a `.deps.yaml` and writes it to `<dir>/.deps.yaml` (`--output` elsewhere, `-` to stdout). The Renovate config is never modified or deleted. An existing output file is only replaced with `--force` (else exit 2).

The config is the first of `renovate.json`, `renovate.jsonc`, `renovate.json5`, the same names under `.github/`, `.gitlab/`, `.gitea/` and `.forgejo/`, `.renovaterc`, `.renovaterc.json(c|5)` and the `renovate` key of `package.json`; `--config` names it explicitly. JSON, JSONC and JSON5 are accepted. Its `extends` presets are resolved: Renovate's built-in presets from a table, `github>`, `gitea>`, `forgejo>` and `local>` presets by fetching them (credentials as for lookups, see `deps help environment`).

`deps plan|apply|run|explain --renovate` run the same translation in memory, so a migrated file behaves exactly like compatibility mode. Settings deps cannot express are listed on stderr as `warn    <setting>: <msg>`, settings without effect on which updates or PRs exist as `info    <setting>: <msg>` (with `-v`); both also head the written file as comments.

- The branch prefix follows Renovate (`renovate/` by default): `deps run` closes open PRs under it that it does not manage, so turn Renovate off before the first run.
- Renovate schedules are time windows, deps schedules are the crons of the workflow triggers that may create PRs. Each entry becomes the cron of the window's start (`* * * * 0` and `before 6am on sunday` become `0 0 * * 0`); the summary lists the crons the workflow's `on.schedule` needs.
- Renovate's regex (`/re/`) and negated (`!pattern`) name, path and file patterns are kept as they are.

The summary line reads `wrote <file> from <renovate config>: <n> rules, <n> custom managers, <n> custom datasources; <n> warnings, <n> notes`.

### deps migrate examples

```sh
deps migrate
deps migrate --config .github/renovate.json5 --output -
```

### deps migrate flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--force` | bool | `false` | overwrite an existing output file |
| `--output` | string | `""` | file to write (default: \<dir>/.deps.yaml; - writes to stdout) |

## deps plan

Print the updates as a unified diff without writing files.

```
deps plan
```

Resolves every dependency and prints the report on stderr (see `deps help output`). Then writes a unified diff per changed file to stdout (`a/<path>` → `b/<path>`); `git apply` accepts it. Nothing is written to the repository.

Post-processors do not run, so `go.sum` and lockfile changes are missing from the diff; `plan` notes this with `note    go.sum changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    package-lock.json changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    Cargo.lock changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    Gemfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    composer.lock changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    Manifest.toml changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    MODULE.bazel.lock changes are computed by apply/run` and `note    .terraform.lock.hcl changes are computed by apply/run`. Use `deps apply` to get them.

A dependency with updates in several PR buckets contributes one update to the files: the newest non-major one, else the lowest major. Its other updates are reported with `, separate PR`, as is the lock file maintenance update (`lockFileMaintenance`), which only `deps run` makes.

The platform is only detected from CI environment variables. Locally, lookups run without a platform token unless one of the token variables is set (see `deps help environment`).

### deps plan examples

```sh
deps plan > deps.diff && git apply --check deps.diff
deps plan -v --dir ../other-repo
deps plan --config ci/deps.yaml --log-level info
```

## deps preview

Compare the PRs a pull request's checkout would get with those of the base branch.

```
deps preview [flags]
```

Resolves two checkouts of the repository, `--dir` (the pull request) and `--base-dir` (its base branch), each with its own `.deps.yaml`, and reports how the update PRs `deps run` would open differ: new PRs, changed PRs (other updates or another title) and PRs no longer opened (open ones would be closed as obsolete). Lookups are shared between the two checkouts, so each release list is fetched once. Nothing is written to the repository or the forge, except the check run below.

Output lines (stderr):

```
new     <branch>  <title>
changed <branch>  <title>
removed <branch>  <title>
error   <message>                    (lookup errors of --dir)
check   <url>                        (the check run, GitHub)
<n> new, <c> changed, <r> no longer opened, <s> the same (<duration>)
```

**Step summary.** The comparison is appended to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (or `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY`) as markdown, with an update table per new or changed PR.

**Check run (GitHub).** In a `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` job on GitHub, deps also creates the completed check run `deps preview` on the pull request's head commit (from the event payload), with the same markdown as its output, so it shows on the PR's *Checks* tab. The conclusion is `success`, or `neutral` when lookups failed: the preview informs and never blocks. Only App installation tokens (`GITHUB_TOKEN` included) can create check runs, with `checks: write`; for a token that can't (a PAT, a fork PR's read-only token), deps prints a `note` and keeps the step summary.

Exit codes: 0 with no lookup errors, 1 with lookup errors, 2 for an invalid config in either checkout.

### deps preview examples

```sh
# in a pull_request job with the PR checked out in pr/ and the base branch in base/
deps preview --dir pr --base-dir base
```

### deps preview flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--base-dir` | string | `""` | checkout of the base branch to compare with (required) |

## deps run

Push one branch and open or update one pull request per dependency or group.

```
deps run [flags]
```

Detects the platform (GitHub, Gitea or Forgejo, from the CI environment, else from the `origin` remote), resolves every dependency, builds one commit per group on a temporary index (no checkout; the working tree is never modified), pushes it with `--force-with-lease`, and creates or updates the PRs. With platform commits (GitHub, see below) the commits are created and the branches moved through the GitHub API instead.

- PRs whose updates all automerge (config key `automerge`) get platform auto-merge requested. With `automergeType: branch` there is no PR: the branch is pushed, and once its checks pass the base branch is fast-forwarded to it (one branch per run); failed checks open the PR.
- With `prCreation: not-pending` or `status-success` the branch is pushed without a PR, and a later run opens the PR once its checks finished or all passed. With `draftPR` new PRs are drafts (GitHub's draft flag; a `WIP: ` title prefix on Gitea and Forgejo, `Draft: ` on GitLab), unless they automerge.
- With `dependencyDashboard`, the dashboard issue is read first (its ticked checkboxes apply to this run) and written last.
- With `lockFileMaintenance`, one more PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance` refreshes every lockfile deps maintains (`Cargo.lock`, npm, pnpm, yarn and bun locks, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `pdm.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `composer.lock`, Julia manifests, `MODULE.bazel.lock`, Gradle lockfiles, `.terraform.lock.hcl`, and the `// indirect` requirements of `go.mod` with `go.sum`) with the ecosystem's tool; it is closed when the lockfiles are current.
- Obsolete PRs of the base under `branchPrefix` are closed and their branches deleted when the base's resolution had no errors, and obsolete branches without any PR (branch automerge, `prCreation`) are deleted when no base had any. PRs to other branches are left alone.
- On an open PR, its ticked rebase checkbox or the `rebaseLabel` (default `rebase`) requests a rebuild like the dashboard's rebase checkbox; deps unticks the box and removes the label afterwards. The `stopUpdatingLabel` (default `stop-updating`) makes deps leave the PR alone.
- With `--base` or the default branch, the local `HEAD` must be the tip of `origin/<base>`.

**Base branches:** `--base`, else the config key `baseBranches`, else the repository's default branch. `baseBranches` lists names, `$default` and `/<RE2>/` regexes over the branches on origin (names origin lacks are skipped with a warning). Each base is resolved from its own tip, with the checkout's config, its `rules[].baseBranches` matching that base: the checkout serves the base it is the tip of, every other base gets a temporary linked work tree of its fetched tip. With more than one entry, or a regex one, branches carry the base (`<branchPrefix><base>/<manager>/<name>`), the log prints `base    <base>` before each base's updates, and the dashboard has a section per base; the PR limits count all bases together. `--base` overrides `baseBranches` with one base and the plain branch names.

**Token:** `--token`, then `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_TOKEN`, then the password from `git credential fill` for the platform host. Without any token, `run` fails with `no token for <host>`, except with `--dry-run`, which uses the API anonymously. Git pushes use the checkout's credentials. On GitLab, PRs are merge requests and `--repo` takes the project path (`group/subgroup/name`).

**Several repositories** (`--repositories`, or `$DEPS_REPOSITORIES`): instead of the checkout in `--dir`, `run` works on each listed repository of the forge in turn, so one job can serve a whole organization. An entry is `owner/name`, or `owner/<glob>` (`path.Match` syntax on the name, e.g. `my-org/*` or `my-org/svc-*`) for the repositories of an organization, else a user, that the token can list (GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo; on GitLab name each project); archived repositories and mirrors are left out, and a repository is run once even if several entries name it. The forge comes from the CI environment, else from the `origin` remote of `--dir` with `--platform`/`--api-url` applying as usual; `--repo` cannot be combined with it. Each repository is cloned shallowly (its default branch, or `--base`) into a temporary directory with the token as git credentials (`AUTHORIZATION: basic` of `x-access-token:<token>`, masked in the CI log), which also push its branches, and is removed afterwards. Its own `.deps.yaml` applies, or the `--config` file for all of them; datasources are shared, so a release list is fetched once for all repositories. Each repository starts with a `repository <owner/name>` line and ends with its own summary and counts line; a repository that fails (clone, config or run errors) does not stop the others, and the run ends with `<n> repositories, <m> failed` (exit 1 when `m` is not 0). In a multi-repository run annotations name the repository instead of a file, and `--report`, the step outputs and the step summary cover all repositories (see `deps help output`). The token needs write access to every repository.

**Author precedence:** an explicitly set `--author-name`/`--author-email`, then `$DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR`, then the config key `gitAuthor`, then the defaults. Each field is resolved separately. An invalid `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR` exits 2. Platform commits ignore it: GitHub authors them as the token's account.

**Platform commits** (config key `platformCommit`, overridden by `$DEPS_PLATFORM_COMMIT`; `auto`, `enabled` or `disabled`): on GitHub, deps uploads the changed files as blobs, creates tree and commit through the REST API on top of the base, and moves the branch with the GraphQL `updateRefs` mutation, compare-and-swap against the tip listed at the start of the run (`stale info` if it moved). GitHub signs commits created with a GitHub App installation token (`ghs_…`, including `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so they show as verified, authored by the App's bot; with other tokens they stay unsigned (warned). `auto` enables them for an App token without a signing key. `enabled` on Gitea/Forgejo, or together with a signing key, exits 2; without a token (`--dry-run`) it falls back to git. Logged at info as `platform commits author=<name> <email>`. A branch tip GitHub links to the token's account, or with the configured git author, counts as deps' own.

**Post-upgrade tasks** (config key `rules[].postUpgradeTasks`) run only when a pattern of `--allow-tasks` (repeatable; `$DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS`, one per line) matches each command whole: `--allow-tasks 'go generate ./...'`, `--allow-tasks 'make *'`, `--allow-tasks '*'`. `*` matches any text except command chaining and substitution (`;`, `&`, `|`, backticks, `$(`, line breaks), so `make *` allows `make docs` but not `make docs; curl …` or `make $(id)`; operators written in the pattern match literally (`echo * >> deps.txt`), and the pattern `*` alone allows every command. Otherwise the group fails before anything runs, naming the command. After the post-processors, each group's commands (once per update with `executionMode: update`, then the branch-mode ones) run in a temporary copy of the work tree holding its changes, which is a throwaway git repository of the base (git works in it; nothing it writes reaches the checkout's repository), and every file below `--dir` they add, change or delete that `.gitignore` does not ignore (and the task's `files` globs match, if set) joins the commit. Submodule content never does, and moving a submodule's HEAD fails the group, as does a failing command. They run repository code; see `docs/ci.md`.

**Commit signing:** with `--signing-key` (or `$DEPS_SIGNING_KEY`), every commit deps creates is signed. The value is the private key itself, as a CI secret holds it, or the path of a file holding it; the format is detected from the armor header:

- `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`: SSH signature (`gpg.format=ssh`) with a `0600` temporary copy of the key; needs `ssh-keygen`.
- `-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----`: OpenPGP signature; the key is imported once into a temporary `GNUPGHOME`; needs `gpg`.

Only keys without a passphrase are supported; a protected key fails before any work is done. The temporary key material is removed when `run` exits, also on errors and on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The key is logged at info by fingerprint only, as `commit signing format=ssh|openpgp key=<fingerprint>`. A value that is neither format nor a readable file exits 2; a missing `ssh-keygen`/`gpg` exits 1. The forge shows the signature as verified only when the committer (`gitAuthor`) is the key owner's verified email. Without a key, git's own configuration applies (`commit.gpgSign` and `user.signingKey` of the checkout).

**Trigger:** cron triggers in `schedule` (crons with a fixed minute) are matched against what started the run, not against the clock: `--trigger-schedule`, then `$DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE`, then `$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` with the `schedule` field of the payload at `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`. `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch` and local runs without CI variables match every trigger. Every other event (`push`, `issues`, `workflow_run`, …) is a maintenance run outside every trigger: only groups without a schedule (and security updates) get new PRs; open PRs are refreshed per `updateNotScheduled`; dashboard checkboxes still act. The value of `--trigger-schedule` is validated as a 5-field cron; an invalid one exits 2.

**Time windows** in `schedule` (`before 6am on monday`, crons with minute `*`) are evaluated against the run time in the config's `timezone`, whatever the event: `--schedule-time` (RFC 3339, e.g. `2026-11-09T05:30:00+01:00`), then `$DEPS_SCHEDULE_TIME`, then now; an invalid value exits 2. Logged at info as `trigger event=<event> cron=<cron> time=<RFC 3339>`.

**New-PR limit:** the minimum of `--max-new-prs` and the room left below `prConcurrentLimit`/`prHourlyLimit`, counting only the non-zero ones. Existing PRs are always updated.

**PR statuses** (the `pr` lines, see `deps help output`; for a group without a PR, branch automerge or waiting for `prCreation`, they describe its branch):

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `created` | new PR, or new branch (branch automerge, `prCreation`) |
| `updated` | content changed or the PR was unmergeable; force-pushed and PR edited. A branch automerge branch is also rebuilt when the base moved |
| `rebased` | unchanged content rebuilt on a moved base (`rebaseWhen: behind-base-branch`), or on request (the PR's rebase checkbox or `rebaseLabel`, or the dashboard) |
| `up-to-date` | nothing to do |
| `closed` | obsolete PR closed and branch deleted |
| `deleted` | obsolete branch without a PR deleted (branch automerge, `prCreation`) |
| `would-create`, `would-update`, `would-rebase` | `--dry-run` |
| `skipped: closed PR for this version` | an unmerged closed PR has the same branch and title, or the same versions of a major update (the dashboard's recreate checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: closed PR for this major` | an unmerged closed PR of the same major branch (`-major`, `-v<N>`) targeted the same majors: closing a major PR ignores that major until the next one (the dashboard's recreate checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: awaiting dashboard approval` | the group needs `dashboardApproval` and has no PR or branch yet: listed under *Pending approval* on the dashboard, whose create checkbox approves it |
| `skipped: outside schedule` | the run was triggered by a cron that is not in the group's `schedule`, or by another event, and no time window of it contains the run time (the dashboard's create checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: new PR limit reached` | a PR limit is exhausted (dashboard checkboxes override it) |
| `skipped: branch modified by someone else` | the branch tip's author is neither the bot nor in `gitIgnoredAuthors` (a rebase request discards those commits) |
| `skipped: stop-updating label` | the open PR has the `stopUpdatingLabel`: not pushed, rebased or closed as obsolete |

**Automerge outcomes** (appended to the PR status, e.g. `created, automerge`):

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `automerge` | platform auto-merge requested (or already scheduled); the forge merges once required checks pass |
| `automerge enabled` | GitHub reports auto-merge enabled already; not requested again |
| `automerge pending` | Gitea/Forgejo cannot schedule it yet (mergeability check of a fresh push still running), or GitLab refused it for now (draft, conflicts, failed or missing required pipeline, approvals, head moved); the next run asks again |
| `automerge waiting for checks` | GitHub will not auto-merge (auto-merge disallowed, or nothing to wait for) and the PR is not mergeable yet or its statuses/check runs are not all green; the next run checks again |
| `merged` | merged directly: the GitHub fallback (mergeable with all statuses and check runs green), or a branch automerge branch fast-forwarded into the base and deleted |
| `branch automerge waiting for checks` | branch automerge: the branch has no PR and its checks have not finished or none are reported; the next run checks again |
| `branch automerge next run` | branch automerge: the checks passed, but another branch was merged in this run or the base moved; the next run rebases or merges it |
| `would-automerge` | `--dry-run` |

**PR creation outcomes** (appended to the status of a branch without a PR under `prCreation: not-pending` or `status-success`, e.g. `created, PR waiting for checks`):

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PR waiting for checks` | the branch's checks have not finished or none are reported; the next run checks again |
| `PR waiting for green checks` | `status-success`: a check failed; the PR is opened once they all pass, or when ticked on the dashboard |

**Dashboard statuses** (the `dashboard` line): `created`, `updated`, `up-to-date` (body unchanged, not edited), `would-create`, `would-update` (`--dry-run`), and `skipped: issues disabled` (the repository has no issue tracker; not an error).

### deps run examples

```sh
# what would happen, without a token and without writes
deps run --dry-run -v
# what the run triggered by the Sunday cron would do
deps run --dry-run --trigger-schedule '0 0 * * 0'
# what a run on Monday 05:30 UTC would do with schedule time windows
deps run --dry-run --schedule-time 2026-11-09T05:30:00Z
# in CI (the action runs this with DEPS_TOKEN set)
DEPS_TOKEN=$TOKEN deps run -v --log-level info
```

### deps run flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--allow-tasks` | strings | `[]` | postUpgradeTasks command allowed to run, `*` matching any text but ; & \| ` $( and line breaks, e.g. `go generate ./...`, `make *` or `*` (repeatable); they run repository code on this machine (default: $DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS, one per line) |
| `--api-url` | string | `""` | API base URL (default: detected) |
| `--author-email` | string | `"deps-bot@noreply.invalid"` | commit author email (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then gitAuthor of the config, then the default) |
| `--author-name` | string | `"deps[bot]"` | commit author name (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then gitAuthor of the config, then the default) |
| `--base` | string | `""` | base branch, overriding baseBranches of the config (default: baseBranches, else the repository's default branch) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | report what would change without pushing or calling write APIs (no PR, merge or issue writes); works without a token |
| `--max-new-prs` | int | `10` | maximum number of pull requests to create per run (0 = unlimited) |
| `--platform` | string | `"auto"` | forge type: auto\|github\|gitea\|forgejo\|gitlab (auto: from the CI environment, else the origin remote) |
| `--repo` | string | `""` | repository owner/name, or the GitLab project path (default: detected) |
| `--repositories` | strings | `[]` | run on these repositories one after another instead of the checkout in --dir, each cloned into a temporary directory with the token: owner/name, or owner/\<glob> (e.g. `my-org/*`, `my-org/svc-*`) for the repositories of an organization or user the token can list (not on GitLab), without archived ones and mirrors (repeatable, comma-separated; default: $DEPS_REPOSITORIES, separated by whitespace or commas) |
| `--schedule-time` | string | `""` | evaluate schedule time windows at this RFC 3339 time instead of now, e.g. 2026-11-09T05:30:00+01:00 (default: $DEPS_SCHEDULE_TIME) |
| `--signing-key` | string | `""` | sign deps' commits with this passphrase-less private key (OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP), given as the key itself or a file path (default: $DEPS_SIGNING_KEY) |
| `--token` | string | `""` | platform API token; git pushes use the checkout's credentials (default: $DEPS_TOKEN, $GITHUB_TOKEN, $GITEA_TOKEN, $FORGEJO_TOKEN, $GITLAB_TOKEN, git credential helper) |
| `--trigger-schedule` | string | `""` | act as if the run was triggered by this workflow cron, overriding $GITHUB_EVENT_NAME/$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH (default: $DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE) |

## deps schema

Print the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of .deps.yaml.

```
deps schema
```

Prints the JSON Schema of `.deps.yaml`, reflected from the config types, with every key's description (`markdownDescription` holds the long form editors show on hover). Unknown keys are rejected (`additionalProperties: false`), as in the loader. The repository's `deps.schema.json` is this output.

### deps schema examples

```sh
deps schema > deps.schema.json
# then start .deps.yaml with:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./deps.schema.json
```

## deps submit

Submit the dependencies to GitHub's dependency graph.

```
deps submit [flags]
```

Extracts every dependency (no lookups, no network apart from the submission) and submits them to GitHub's dependency graph as one snapshot (the [dependency submission API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/dependency-submission)): one manifest per file, one package URL per dependency. GitHub then shows them in *Insights → Dependency graph*, includes them in the SBOM export and in dependency review, and raises Dependabot alerts for the ecosystems of its advisory database.

**What is submitted.** By default only the files GitHub does not read by itself: Gradle builds and version catalogs, the Maven and Gradle wrappers, Dockerfiles, Compose files, Kubernetes and Helm YAML and other image references, custom (annotation and regex) dependencies, and the other managers whose datasource has a package URL type. go.mod, package.json, the Python manifests, Cargo.toml, pom.xml and workflows are left out, because GitHub parses them itself (with the full resolved graph for Go and Python) and a submitted manifest replaces GitHub's view of that file; `--all-managers` submits them too.

**Package URLs** by datasource: `go` → `pkg:golang/<module>`, `npm` → `pkg:npm/<name>` (`%40scope/name`), `pypi` → `pkg:pypi/<name>`, `crate` → `pkg:cargo/<name>`, `maven` → `pkg:maven/<group>/<artifact>`, `github-releases` (github.com) → `pkg:github/<owner>/<repo>`, `docker` → `pkg:docker/<path>` (with `?repository_url=<registry>` outside Docker Hub), GitHub Actions → `pkg:githubactions/<owner>/<repo>`; the version is the locked one when a lockfile has it, else the one written. Deps without a concrete version (ranges, variables, templates) and datasources without a purl type (helm, terraform, node and Go toolchain versions, git tags) are left out. Deps ignored by policy (ignored by default, or by a rule) are real dependencies and are submitted. Every dependency is `direct`; `devDependencies`, dev groups and `test` deps have scope `development`, the rest `runtime`.

**Snapshot fields**: `job.correlator` is `<GITHUB_WORKFLOW> <GITHUB_JOB> deps`, so each workflow job keeps its own latest snapshot; `job.id` is `GITHUB_RUN_ID`; `sha` and `ref` are `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF`; the detector is `deps` with its version.

The token needs `contents: write` (`GITHUB_TOKEN` works). Outside GitHub Actions, and on Gitea and Forgejo, `submit` exits 2; `--dry-run` prints the snapshot as JSON to stdout instead, anywhere.

Output lines (stderr): `manifest  <file>  <count>` per manifest, `submitted <result>` (`SUCCESS`, or `ACCEPTED` when GitHub queues it), `error   <message>` per file that failed to parse, and `<n> dependencies in <m> manifests, <e> errors`.

### deps submit examples

```sh
# in a GitHub Actions job with contents: write
deps submit
# print the snapshot instead of submitting it
deps submit --dry-run > snapshot.json
```

### deps submit flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all-managers` | bool | `false` | also submit the manifests GitHub reads by itself (go.mod, package.json, Python, Cargo, pom.xml, workflows); a submitted manifest replaces GitHub's own view of that file |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | print the snapshot JSON to stdout instead of submitting it; works outside GitHub Actions |

## deps version

Print the deps version.

```
deps version
```

Prints the version set at build time with `-ldflags "-X main.version=<v>"` (`dev` otherwise). Release binaries print their tag, e.g. `v0.1.0`; the action prints it after download.

## Environment

Environment variables deps reads. Also shown by `deps help environment`.

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_TOKEN` | all | platform token, first non-empty wins; `run --token` takes precedence. `run` falls back to `git credential fill` for the platform host, and without any token fails with `no token for <host>` (except `--dry-run`). Sent to the platform host's lookups as Basic `x-access-token:<token>` (`oauth2:<token>` on GitLab). |
| `DEPS_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` | all | token for github.com lookups when the platform is not github.com (avoids anonymous rate limits for actions and releases hosted on GitHub) |
| `DEPS_DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL` | all | default host of `owner/repo@ref` actions (hostname, or a URL whose host is used); overridden by the config key `actions.defaultHost` |
| `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN` | `gitlabci` manager, `git-tags` datasource | token for the GitLab instance's host (see `CI_SERVER_URL`), sent as Basic `oauth2:<token>`; a platform token for the same host takes precedence |
| `CI_SERVER_URL`, `CI_SERVER_HOST`, `CI_JOB_TOKEN` | `gitlabci` manager, `git-tags` datasource | set by GitLab CI. `CI_SERVER_URL` is the GitLab instance URL unless the config key `gitlabci.url` sets one (else the server of a GitLab platform `run` detected from the remote, else `https://gitlab.com`). Without `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN`, `CI_JOB_TOKEN` is sent as Basic `gitlab-ci-token:<token>` when `CI_SERVER_HOST` (else `CI_SERVER_URL`'s host) is the instance's host. |
| `GITLAB_CI`, `CI_API_V4_URL`, `CI_PROJECT_PATH` | all | set by GitLab CI: `GITLAB_CI=true` makes GitLab the platform, with `CI_SERVER_URL` as server, `CI_API_V4_URL` as API (default `<server>/api/v4`) and `CI_PROJECT_PATH` as repository |
| `DEPS_NODE_DIST_URL` | `node-version` datasource | base URL of a nodejs.org `dist` mirror (default `https://nodejs.org/dist`) |
| `TF_TOKEN_<host>` | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | registry token sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to `<host>` (dots as `_`, hyphens as `__`, e.g. `TF_TOKEN_app_terraform_io`), as the Terraform CLI reads it; takes precedence over the CLI config |
| `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE`, `TERRAFORM_CONFIG` | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | Terraform CLI config read for registry `credentials` blocks and the `credentials_helper`, replacing `~/.terraformrc` (`%APPDATA%/terraform.rc`); when set, the `*.tfrc`/`*.tfrc.json` files of `~/.terraform.d` (`credentials.tfrc.json`) are not read. `TERRAFORM_CONFIG` is the legacy name |
| `HOME`, `APPDATA` (Windows) | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | where the Terraform CLI config, `credentials.tfrc.json` and credentials helpers (`.terraform.d/plugins`) are found |
| `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR` | `run` | commit author `Name <email>`; between the `--author-*` flags and the config key `gitAuthor`; ignored for platform commits |
| `DEPS_SIGNING_KEY` | `run` | default of `--signing-key`: a passphrase-less OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP private key, or the path of a file holding one; deps signs its commits with it |
| `DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS` | `apply`, `run` | default of `--allow-tasks`: the `postUpgradeTasks` commands that may run (repository code), one pattern per line, `*` matching any text without `;`, `&`, `|`, backticks, `$(` or line breaks (`go generate ./...`, `make *`; `*` alone allows everything). Commands get the environment without `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_TOKEN`, `DEPS_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`, `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN`, `CI_JOB_TOKEN`, `DEPS_SIGNING_KEY`, and without `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` and `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, so their git uses the repository they run in |
| `DEPS_PLATFORM_COMMIT` | `run` | `auto`, `enabled` or `disabled`; overrides the config key `platformCommit` (commits through the GitHub API, see `deps help run`). Renovate's `RENOVATE_PLATFORM_COMMIT` |
| `DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE` | `run` | default of `--trigger-schedule` |
| `DEPS_SCHEDULE_TIME` | `run` | default of `--schedule-time`: the RFC 3339 time schedule time windows are evaluated at instead of now |
| `DEPS_REPOSITORIES` | `run` | default of `--repositories`: `owner/name` and `owner/<glob>` entries separated by whitespace or commas |
| `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` | `run` | run trigger and its payload (cron of `schedule` events); set by GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo runners |
| `DEPS_LOG_LEVEL`, `DEPS_LOG_FORMAT` | all | defaults of `--log-level`, `--log-format` |
| `RUNNER_DEBUG` | all | `1` (an Actions re-run with debug logging) makes `debug` the default `--log-level`, below `DEPS_LOG_LEVEL` and the flag |
| `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `FORCE_COLOR` | all | with `--color auto`: `NO_COLOR` (any value) or `TERM=dumb` turn colors off on a terminal; `CLICOLOR_FORCE` or `FORCE_COLOR` (any value but `0` or `false`) turn them on, also when piped and over `NO_COLOR`. `--color always`/`never` ignore them |
| `DEPS_REPORT` | `plan`, `apply`, `run` | default of `--report` (JSON report file, see `deps help output`) |
| `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, `npm_config_registry` | `npm` datasource | registry when no `.npmrc` sets one (default `https://registry.npmjs.org/`) |
| `DOCKER_CONFIG` | `docker` datasource | directory of the Docker `config.json` with registry credentials and credential helpers (default `~/.docker`) |
| `DEPS_CRATES_INDEX_URL`, `DEPS_CRATES_API_URL` | `crate` datasource | base URLs of a crates.io sparse index mirror (default `https://index.crates.io`) and of the crates.io API used for source repositories (default `https://crates.io`) |
| `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_INDEX`, `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN`, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` | `crate` datasource | alternative registries: Cargo's config (`$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, default `~/.cargo`, after the `.cargo/config.toml` files from the manifest up to `--dir`) and credentials (`$CARGO_HOME/credentials.toml`); the variables override them as in Cargo. A registry token is sent as `Authorization` only to its index host; without one, the platform token (for its host) and, after a 401, `git credential fill` are used |
| `PIP_INDEX_URL` | `pypi` datasource | index when the manifest names none (simple API, JSON or HTML) |
| `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL` | `pypi` datasource | space-separated extra indexes searched for every Python dep after the manifest's own; their releases are merged in |
| `DEPS_PYPI_URL` | `pypi` datasource | base of the PyPI JSON API (default `https://pypi.org`) |
| `DEPS_RUBY_RELEASES_URL` | `ruby-version` datasource | URL of the Ruby release list (YAML entries with `version` and `date`; default `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruby/www.ruby-lang.org/master/_data/releases.yml`) |
| `DEPS_CONDA_URL` | `conda` datasource | base of the anaconda.org API (default `https://api.anaconda.org`) |
| `DEPS_PACKAGIST_URL` | `packagist` datasource | base of Packagist's metadata API (`/p2/<name>.json`), also for composer.json repositories naming `https://packagist.org` or `https://repo.packagist.org` (default `https://repo.packagist.org`) |
| `COMPOSER_AUTH` | `packagist` datasource | Composer's auth.json as JSON: `http-basic` (`{"repo.example.com": {"username": "…", "password": "…"}}`) and `bearer` (`{"repo.example.com": "<token>"}`) credentials by host for composer repositories; `composer update` reads it too |
| `DEPS_RUBYGEMS_URL` | `rubygems` datasource | base of the rubygems.org API, also for Gemfiles naming `https://rubygems.org` (default `https://rubygems.org`) |
| `DEPS_RUST_MANIFESTS_URL` | `rust-version` datasource | URL of the Rust manifest index (one `…/dist/<date>/channel-rust-<version>.toml` URL per line; default `https://static.rust-lang.org/manifests.txt`) |
| `DEPS_ELM_PACKAGE_URL` | `elm-package` datasource | base of the Elm package registry API (default `https://package.elm-lang.org`) |
| `DEPS_JULIA_REGISTRY_URL` | `julia-registry` datasource | raw file base of the Julia registry (default `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliaRegistries/General/HEAD`; a mirror or another registry with General's layout, userinfo sent as basic auth) |
| `BUNDLE_<HOST>` | `rubygems` datasource | Bundler's credentials for a gem server (`gems.example-corp.com` → `BUNDLE_GEMS__EXAMPLE___CORP__COM`): `user:password`, or a token; sent as basic auth to that host only |
| `DEPS_CIRCLECI_URL`, `DEPS_CIRCLECI_TOKEN` | `orb` datasource | CircleCI host of the orb registry (default `https://circleci.com`; CircleCI server), and an API token for private orbs, sent as `Circle-Token` and bare `Authorization` to that host |
| `DEPS_AZURE_PIPELINES_TASKS_URL` | `azure-pipelines-tasks` datasource | base of the public task lists `azure-pipelines-builtin-tasks.json` and `azure-pipelines-marketplace-tasks.json` (default `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renovatebot/azure-devops-marketplace/main`) |
| `DEPS_AZURE_DEVOPS_URL`, `DEPS_AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN` | `azure-pipelines-tasks` datasource | both set: the task versions are those installed in this Azure DevOps organization or collection (`https://dev.azure.com/<org>`), listed with the personal access token as basic auth, instead of the public lists |
| `DEPS_BAZEL_REGISTRY_URL` | `bazel` datasource | Bazel Central Registry base (a mirror), also where `.bazelrc` names `https://bcr.bazel.build` (default `https://bcr.bazel.build`) |
| `DEPS_NUGET_URL` | `nuget` datasource | service index read for nuget.org, also where a nuget.config names `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json` (default that URL; a mirror serving the v3 API) |
| `NuGetPackageSourceCredentials_<key>` | `nuget` datasource | NuGet's credentials of the nuget.config package source `<key>`: `Username=<user>;Password=<token>`; sent as basic auth to that source's host only |
| `DEPS_DOTNET_RELEASES_URL` | `dotnet-version` datasource | URL of the .NET release metadata index (default `https://builds.dotnet.microsoft.com/dotnet/release-metadata/releases-index.json`); the channels' `releases.json` URLs come from it |
| `GOPROXY`, `GONOPROXY`, `GOPRIVATE`, `GOMODCACHE` | `go` datasource | read via `go env -json` (the process environment when `go` is not on `PATH`). `GOMODCACHE`'s `cache/download/**/@v/*.info` files provide release times without network. |
| `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITEA_ACTIONS`, `FORGEJO_ACTIONS`, `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, `GITHUB_API_URL`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `FORGEJO_SERVER_URL`, `FORGEJO_API_URL`, `FORGEJO_REPOSITORY` | all | platform detection: `FORGEJO_ACTIONS=true` → forgejo, `GITEA_ACTIONS=true` → gitea, `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` → github; the `FORGEJO_*` variables fall back to the `GITHUB_*` ones. `GITHUB_ACTIONS` or `GITEA_ACTIONS` without `FORGEJO_ACTIONS` also makes `--log-format auto` the `actions` format (workflow commands). `run` also detects from the `origin` remote; `plan`, `apply` and `explain` only from these variables. |
| `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY` | all | step summary file (see `deps help output`) |
| `GITHUB_OUTPUT` | `plan`, `apply`, `run` | step outputs file: the counts are appended (see `deps help output`) |
| `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` | all | on GitHub Actions, annotation paths are made relative to it |

On a 401 without a static token, git tag lookups call `git credential fill` once per host, with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and a 10s timeout. Every `git` process deps runs has `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so deps never prompts. npm lookups use `.npmrc` `_authToken` entries, PyPI index lookups the index URL's userinfo (`https://user:token@host/simple`), and docker lookups the Docker credential chain (`~/.docker/config.json` and credential helpers).

Docker Hub limits anonymous pulls per IP address (`ratelimit-limit: 100;w=3600` at the time of writing) and counts every manifest GET; HEADs are free. deps resolves digests with HEADs and fetches a manifest only for release times. In repositories with many Docker Hub images, or on shared runner IPs, log in (`docker login`, or credentials for `docker.io` in `$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json`). An exhausted quota fails the affected lookups at once with `rate limited by registry-1.docker.io`, instead of retrying until the window ends.

## Exit codes

Exit codes of every command. Also shown by `deps help exit-codes`.

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `0` | success, no errors |
| `1` | any error, including per-dependency lookup errors and per-PR errors (already printed as `error` lines), or a fatal error printed as `deps: <err>` |
| `2` | usage error: bad flag or argument, invalid `--log-level`/`--log-format`/`--platform`/`--concurrency`, invalid `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR`, invalid `--trigger-schedule`/`DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE` or `--schedule-time`/`DEPS_SCHEDULE_TIME`, a `--signing-key`/`DEPS_SIGNING_KEY` that is no OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP private key, an invalid `DEPS_PLATFORM_COMMIT`, `platformCommit: enabled` on Gitea/Forgejo or with a signing key, or any config error (parse error, unknown key, failed validation, unreadable `--config` file) |

## Output

Report lines, summary lines, diagnostics and the CI step summary. Also shown by `deps help output`.

Results go to stderr (the diff of `plan` and the report of `explain` go to stdout), in fixed-width lines:

```
update  <file>:<line>  <name>  <from> -> <to>  (<type>[, lockfile][, separate PR])[  security: <id>,<id>]
update  <lockfile>  lock file maintenance  (lockFileMaintenance, separate PR)   (with lockFileMaintenance)
skip    <file>:<line>  <name>  <reason>                       (with -v)
error   <message>
note    go.sum changes are computed by apply/run              (plan, when a gomod update exists)
note    package-lock.json changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when an npm update exists)
note    Cargo.lock changes are computed by apply/run          (plan, when a cargo update exists)
note    uv.lock, poetry.lock, pdm.lock and Pipfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a Python update exists)
note    pip-compile output and --hash lines of requirements files are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a compiled requirements file, an input of one or a requirements file with --hash has an update)
note    .terraform.lock.hcl changes are computed by apply/run (plan, when a terraform update exists)
note    Gemfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run        (plan, when a bundler update exists)
note    composer.lock changes are computed by apply/run       (plan, when a composer update exists)
note    Manifest.toml changes are computed by apply/run       (plan, when a julia update exists)
note    MODULE.bazel.lock changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a bazel-module update exists)
pr      <status>[, <automerge>]  <branch>  <title>  <url>     (run)
dashboard <status>  <title>  <url>                            (run, with dependencyDashboard)
```

- For digest and pin updates, `<from>`/`<to>` read `<version>@<sha7>`. A lockfile-only update (`, lockfile`) starts at the locked version and changes only the lockfile.
- Per-dependency errors read `<file>:<line>: <name>: <err>`; a fatal error is printed as `deps: <err>`.
- The PR, automerge and dashboard statuses are listed in `deps run --help`; the skip reasons in the managers reference.

**Summary lines:**

```
<n> updates in <m> files, <k> skipped, <e> errors                                                (plan, apply)
<c> created, <u> updated, <x> closed, <s> up-to-date, <k> skipped, <a> automerge, <e> errors     (run)
... (dry run: <w> would change, <m> would automerge)                                              (run --dry-run, appended)
```

`rebased` counts as updated, `deleted` (obsolete branches without a PR) as closed. `<a>` counts auto-merge requests and direct merges, branch merges included (`automerge`, `merged`); the dashboard line is not counted.

**On a terminal** (stderr is a TTY) the `update` lines are left out: the summary block below lists the same updates, grouped by the PR they go to. Everything else is printed as above. Piped or redirected stderr always gets the line format above, byte for byte, so scripts and CI logs see no change. With colors (`--color`, default `auto`: on a terminal unless `NO_COLOR` is set or `TERM=dumb`, and with the `actions` format unless `NO_COLOR` is set; `CLICOLOR_FORCE` or `FORCE_COLOR` force them, also when piped) `error` is red and the summary colors the branches, `<file>:<line>` (dim), the update types (major red, minor yellow, patch green, digest cyan), security advisories (bold red) and the error count (red). Colors never change the layout; `--color always` keeps the piped layout.

Also on a terminal (unless `TERM=dumb`), a **status line** below the output shows the running phase while it runs, e.g. `⠹ resolving 212/308 · npm 18 in flight · 2.1s`: discovering files, extracting (files), resolving (dependencies) and, in `run`, PRs (groups handled), with the requests in flight per upstream pool (`--concurrency`), a rate-limit wait (`rate limited by <host>, <n>s`) and the error count. It is redrawn ten times a second, kept below every log record and removed when the phase ends, so it never stays in the output. Piped stderr never gets it.

**Diagnostics** are written with `log/slog` to stderr, filtered by `--log-level` and formatted by `--log-format`: `auto` (the default) is `actions` on a GitHub or Gitea Actions runner (below), else `pretty` on a terminal and `text` otherwise; `text` is `slog`'s `time=… level=INFO msg=… key=value` format; `json` one JSON object per record; `pretty` a compact line per record for people, `  3.55s WRN <message>  key=value …`: the time since deps started, right-aligned, a three-letter level (`DBG`, `INF`, `WRN`, `ERR`, colored with colors on), the message and the attributes (dim; grouped keys as `group.key`), durations rounded to 0.1ms below a second, else to the millisecond. Records and result lines are written whole, never interleaved. `run` builds up to four PRs at a time; the records of each PR (its build, lockfile tools, push and API calls) are held back and written as one block when the PR is done, so they never interleave with another PR's. What each level logs:

- `debug`: every HTTP request (credential-free URL), every `git`/`go`/`npm`/`cargo` process, credential-helper outcomes (never secrets), and per-dependency and per-PR decisions.
- `info`: the run trigger (`run`), the detected platform and how it was detected, the actions default host and its source (`actions default host host=<h> source=<s>`), phase counts and durations (one `files discovered files=<n> duration=<d> managers="docker 137, helm 134"` line for the walk, listing managers that matched files by count), and the bot's view of the repository.
- `warn` (the default): obsolete PRs left open because the run had errors, a schedule event whose cron cannot be read (every cron trigger matches), a dashboard skipped because issues are disabled, and dashboard labels that do not exist (Gitea/Forgejo).

Text logs round durations to 0.1ms below a second and to 1ms above (`duration=23ms`, `duration=11.003s`); JSON logs keep them in nanoseconds.

**Summary block.** Before the summary line, a block starting with an empty line and `Summary: ` gives the overview:

```
Summary: <n> dependencies, <u> updates in <g> PRs[, PRs: <count> <status>, ...][, <p> held back by minimumReleaseAge], <k> skipped, <e> errors (<duration>)
  PR <branch>  <title>  [<status> <url>; <automerge>; waiting for <schedule entries>]   (run; plan/apply: [automerge; schedule <entries>])
      <name>  <file>:<line>  <from> -> <to>  (<type>[, security: <id>,...])
  <status>  <branch>  <url>                                            (run: closed obsolete PRs and the dashboard)
  Held back by minimumReleaseAge:
      <name>  <file>:<line>  <version>  too new (released <date>, minimum <age>) | release time unknown (minimum <age>, timestamp-required)
  Deprecated or abandoned: <n> (-v lists each)
      <name>  <file>:<line>  deprecated: <reason> | abandoned: <reason>   (with -v)
  Skipped (-v lists each dependency):
    <count>  <reason>  (<how to update>)
```

The PRs are the ones `run` opens: plan and apply group their updates the same way. Without updates, errors or PR actions, the headline reads `No updates: <n> dependencies up to date, <k> skipped.` Errors are not repeated; they are the `error` lines above.

**Step summary.** If `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (or else `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY`) is set, the same summary is appended to that file as markdown, under `## deps <command>`: the headline, one section per PR with its branch, status and link (run), automerge and schedule, and a `| Dependency | File | From | To | Type |` table; other PR actions (closed PRs, the dashboard); held-back releases; skip reasons with counts and how to update, with the skipped dependencies in a collapsible `<details>`; and the errors in full. The file stays within GitHub's 1 MiB per step, counting what is already in it: when the summary does not fit, the list of skipped dependencies is left out first, then the held-back releases, then the PRs' update tables; if it still does not fit, it is cut and ends with a note pointing at the job log.

**Actions workflow commands.** With `--log-format actions`, which `auto` selects on GitHub Actions (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`) and Gitea Actions (`GITEA_ACTIONS=true`; Gitea 1.26 and later render groups and annotation lines) but not on Forgejo (`FORGEJO_ACTIONS=true`, which prints workflow commands literally), records are `pretty` lines without the elapsed time (the runner timestamps every line), `INF <message>  key=value …`, colored unless `NO_COLOR` is set or `--color never` is given (GitHub and Gitea render ANSI colors; the result lines keep the piped layout, the summary is colored as on a terminal), and deps also prints workflow commands: each `error` line and a fatal error as an `::error` annotation, located at the dependency's file and line, at the file for a file that cannot be read or parsed, or for config errors at the line of the offending key in `.deps.yaml`; `warn` and `error` logs as `::warning`/`::error`; each security update as a `::notice` at its file and line; the `-v` skip lines inside a collapsible `::group::`; every phase as a group (`Discovering and extracting dependency files`, `Resolving <n> dependencies`) holding its records, a `deps: <phase> <done>/<total> · … · <seconds>s` line every 30 seconds while it runs (when stderr is no terminal) and one when it ends; and in `run` the records of each PR as a group `<branch>: <status> (<duration>)` (groups do not nest, so the PR phase has none of its own; its heartbeat and final lines stand between the PR groups). A token deps gets from the git credential helper is masked (`::add-mask::`) before it is used. GitHub shows 10 error, 10 warning and 10 notice annotations per step, so deps prints no more than that; the result lines are complete. Any other `--log-format` prints no workflow commands, also on a runner. With `RUNNER_DEBUG=1` (a re-run with debug logging) the default `--log-level` is `debug`; `$DEPS_LOG_LEVEL` and the flag still win.

**JSON report.** `--report <file>` (or `$DEPS_REPORT`) makes `plan`, `apply` and `run` also write the summary as one JSON object, replacing the file. It is not written when deps fails before it has a result (usage or config errors, exit 2). Fields:

- `command` (`plan`, `apply`, `run`, `run --dry-run`), `dependencies`, `durationMs`;
- `prs[]`: `branch`, `title`, `updates[]` (`name`, `manager`, `file`, `line`, `from`, `to`, `type`, `lockfile`, `advisories` as IDs; a lock file maintenance has type `lockFileMaintenance` and no versions); for `run` also `status`, `automerge`, `prWait` (the PR creation outcome of a branch waiting for its checks), `number`, `url`, `waitsFor` (schedule entries: crons and time windows) and `reason` (why a `skipped: update cannot be applied` update cannot be applied; the label of a `skipped: stop-updating label` PR);
- `otherActions[]`: closed obsolete PRs, obsolete PRs kept open by the `stopUpdatingLabel`, and the dashboard (`branch`, `title`, `status`, `number`, `url`, `dashboard`);
- `heldBack[]` (`name`, `file`, `line`, `version`, `reason`), `warnings[]` (`name`, `file`, `line`, `kind` `deprecated` or `abandoned`, `reason`; see `abandonmentThreshold` and the dependency dashboard), `skipped[]` (`reason`, `count`), `errors[]` (`message`, plus `file` and `line` for a dependency's lookup error, `file` for a file that cannot be read or parsed);
- `counts`: the step outputs below, by camelCase name.

With `run --repositories` the file holds the whole run: `command`, `durationMs`, `repositories[]` (the object above per repository, with `repository` set to its `owner/name`), `errors[]` (repositories that failed before they had a result, a clone or config error, as `<owner/name>: <message>`) and `counts` summed over the repositories (a failed repository counts as one error).

**Step outputs.** If `GITHUB_OUTPUT` is set (GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo runners), deps appends `updates`, `prs`, `held-back`, `skipped` and `errors`, and for `run` also `created`, `updated` (including rebased), `closed` (including deleted branches), `up-to-date`, `automerged` (auto-merge requests and direct merges) and `prs-skipped` (any `skipped: …` status), each as `<name>=<count>`. The dashboard is not counted. `run --repositories` appends them once, summed over its repositories; its step summary has one `## deps run: <owner/name>` section per repository.
